NOT JUST A LOG

You log a set.

Eighty kilos for eight. In a tracker, that is a row in a table and the end of it.

MetalArm scores it.

Points land on the set itself, weighted by how hard it was - and again when it beats your best.

It tells you what to try next.

Double progression, with a plateau backing you off and a hard month earning a deload.

And it says something.

"That rep looked easy. It wasn't." A record is a moment, not a green cell in a spreadsheet.

The dashboard

The summary

THE MOMENT IT CLICKS

Ninety seconds, counting.

The rest timer runs while you sit there, because the rest is part of the set. It knows how long this movement wants - four minutes under a heavy bar, sixty seconds on a carry - from the workout you picked.

Scroll to watch it run.

Pick how you train. Once.

Asked once, right after you sign up, and changeable any time from your profile. It sets the reps, the loads and the rest the app suggests - and the workouts it leads with. It never touches your points or your rank.

  • Athletic

    12-20 reps · light · short rests

  • Bodybuilder

    8-15 reps · moderate-heavy · moderate rests

  • Powerlifter

    1-6 reps · heavy · long rests

Six tiers. The last one takes years.

Untrained, Novice, Intermediate, Advanced, Elite, World Class. Each promotion is louder than the last - and the top two are held by your streak, so they can be lost as well as won.

Scroll to play.

Proof, not vibes.

Every set you log goes into the record. Heaviest, best estimated one-rep max, most reps - per movement, with the date you did it.

Chart and records as the app draws them, from its demo account's bench press. Real software, real numbers, a made-up lifter.

Nobody trains harder alone.

  • Parties

    Up to ten lifters, a shared quest board, and a leaderboard of what each of you contributed.

  • Duels

    Head to head over a window you choose - volume, sets or sessions. No one to challenge? Your rival is paced from your own recent weeks.

  • The feed

    Your party's records, rank-ups, finished sessions and duel wins, as they happen.

  • Weekly leagues

    Twenty lifters, one week, promotion and relegation. Standings are summed from the ledger, so they cannot drift.

  • Raids

    A weekly boss with health scaled to your party. Every qualified workout lands a hit; idle days heal it.

Your rival never skips a session.

Challenge it when there is nobody else to challenge. Its pace comes from your own recent weeks - never another lifter's data - stretched just far enough to be worth beating.

And after every set, the app tells you what to try next: add a rep, add the smallest jump you can load, or back off, depending on what your last few sessions actually did.
